about: The guide's lessons (S16, S17): data the lesson runner walks the learner through, attached to an NPC. Step types: explain, model, listen, repeat, answer, do, recap (see LessonBook for the fields of each; a do step may name a noun to point the beacon at). Every step has a skip and a help path; a failed or uncertain turn moves on after the step's attempts (fail-forward, D-game-9). Lines are pre-rendered speech ids (speech/<id>.wav); phrases are rows of content/PHRASES.md; a repeat or answer step's prompt must allow the phrase's intent. S17 retired the two-step sample: this is the guide's first lesson, six short units (about eight minutes), and it starts by itself when the player first talks to her. The English thins from a phrase's second use.

lessons.title: First words with Luna
lessons.english: Six short units: hello, yes and no, what is this, please and thank you, getting unstuck, and what the camp needs. About eight minutes.

steps.english: This is Luna, the guide. She will teach you some Spanish, one phrase at a time. Nothing here is a test. Enter goes on, H helps, K skips a step.
Luna waves and says hello.
Say hello back: “Hola” (OH-lah). Hold V to speak into the microphone, or press W to type.
steps.help: Say: Hola (OH-lah). It means hello. The letter h is silent in Spanish.
steps.retry: Not quite. Say: Hola. It means hello.

steps.english: Luna tells you her name. “Me llamo” means “my name is”. You only need to understand this one, not say it.
Next: yes and no. Luna holds things up and asks about them. Answer “Sí” for yes or “No” for no.
Luna holds up a log of wood and asks if it is wood. “Madera” means wood.
It is wood, so the answer is yes. Say “Sí” (SEE).
steps.help: Say: Sí (SEE, with an accent mark). It means yes.
steps.retry: Not quite. It is wood, so say: Sí.

steps.english: She holds up the same log and asks if it is water. It is not: answer “No”.
steps.retry: Not quite. A log is not water, so say: No.

steps.english: Now ask what things are. “¿Qué es esto?” means “What is this?”. Luna points at something and names it.
Luna points at a log. Ask her: “¿Qué es esto?” (keh ehs EHS-toh).
steps.help: Say: ¿Qué es esto? It means what is this?

steps.english: “Esto es” means “this is”. “Madera” is wood.
Luna points at some fruit. Ask again.

steps.translation: This is a piece of fruit.
steps.english: Fruta is fruit.
Luna holds up a bottle of water.
Agua is water.
She taps the bottle: botella.
Luna pats the workbench beside her. What does she say?
steps.help: “Mesa” is a table. The workbench next to Luna is a mesa.
steps.retry: Not quite. Listen again: she pats the workbench.

steps.english: Luna lifts a torch. What does she say?
steps.help: “Antorcha” is a torch. You will make one soon.

steps.english: Good manners. When someone offers you something, “Sí, por favor” means “yes, please”, and “Gracias” means “thank you”.
Luna offers you some fruit. “Quieres” means “do you want”.
You would like some. Say: “Sí, por favor” (SEE, por fah-VOR).
steps.help: Say: Sí, por favor. It means yes, please.
steps.retry: Not quite. Say: Sí, por favor.

steps.english: Luna nods at the berry bushes. You pick the fruit yourself.

steps.hud: Pick a fruit from a berry bush, then go back to Luna
steps.english: Press Esc to close this panel. Aim the dot at a berry bush (the arrow shows one) and hold the left mouse button to pick a fruit. Then walk back to Luna and press E.
steps.help: A berry bush is a green bush with red berries. Hold the left mouse button until the fruit drops into your bar.

steps.english: You have the fruit. Thank Luna: say “Gracias” (GRAH-see-ahs).
steps.help: Say: Gracias. It means thank you.
steps.retry: Not quite. Say: Gracias. It means thank you.

steps.english: “De nada” is the polite answer to “gracias”.
Everyone gets stuck. Three phrases always help: “No sé” (I don't know), “Otra vez, por favor” (again, please) and “Más despacio, por favor” (more slowly, please). The buttons R, S and N do the same.
Luna asks you something and you have no idea. Say “No sé” (noh SEH). It is never wrong.
steps.help: Say: No sé. It means I don't know.
steps.retry: Say: No sé. It means I don't know.

steps.english: When you say “No sé”, Luna tells you the answer.

steps.translation: Look. The wood is for the torch.
steps.english: Luna says something longer. Did you catch it?
Ask her to say it again: “Otra vez, por favor” (OH-trah behs, por fah-VOR). She will repeat her last line.
steps.help: Say: Otra vez, por favor. It means again, please.
steps.retry: Not quite. Say: Otra vez, por favor.

steps.english: Now ask for it more slowly: “Más despacio, por favor” (mahs deh-SPAH-see-oh). She will say it slowly.
steps.help: Say: Más despacio, por favor. It means more slowly, please.
steps.retry: Not quite. Say: Más despacio, por favor.

steps.english: Luna explains what the camp needs. What does she say?
options: She needs a torch and a bottle.
steps.help: “Necesito” is “I need”. “Madera” is wood and “frutas” is fruit.
steps.retry: Not quite. Listen again: madera and frutas.

steps.english: Your list is at the top right: 5 wood, 3 fruit, a torch and water. Collect wood from trees and fruit from bushes (hold the left mouse button). Make a torch at the workbench (press E on it) and place it on the fire ring. The village down the road has water. Talk to Luna any time.
You can already say all of this.
